metric_model: CHAOSS AI Alignment - Community Governed Use

scope.note: Scoring confined to the files named on the command line; 'no' means not addressed in those files.

domains.accountability_wording: contributors remain responsible for the accuracy, completeness, and intent of what they submit

evidence.quote: Review AI-generated code closely before marking a pull request ready for review.
AI may be used to help draft issues and pull requests, but contributors remain responsible for the accuracy, completeness, and intent of what they submit.

domains.reasoning: The 'AI Contribution Policy' section explicitly names pull requests and issues, requires human review/testing before submission (human_in_the_loop), requires disclosure, and states contributors bear responsibility for accuracy/completeness/intent of what they submit, giving both a supervision level and an accountability holder.

domains.suggested_improvement: no mention of meeting/notetaker bots; no supervision level or holder
domains.reasoning: CONTRIBUTING.md contains no reference to meeting recording, notetaker bots, or closed/small-group discussion capture.

domains.suggested_improvement: no rule for AI use in documentation/blogs/design assets
domains.reasoning: The AI policy section is framed around pull requests and issues (code contributions); the Documentation section of CONTRIBUTING.md makes no mention of AI at all, so non-code content is unaddressed.

domains.rationale_only_mention: We welcome new contributors, but cannot sustain the effort of supporting contributors who primarily defer to AI rather than engaging substantively with the review process.
domains.suggested_improvement: no supervision level or accountability holder for moderation actions
domains.reasoning: The clause about maintainers 'reserving the right to close' non-compliant PRs is enforcement of the code-contribution disclosure rule, not a statement about AI being used for moderation, and the effort/sustainability sentence is a rationale about reviewer workload rather than a rule for the moderation domain.

domains.suggested_improvement: no rule on AI use by reviewers evaluating contributions
domains.reasoning: The policy requires the contributor to review their own AI-generated code before submission, but says nothing about whether maintainers/reviewers themselves may use AI tools when reviewing a PR.

domains.suggested_improvement: no rule on autonomous/agentic interaction with the repository
domains.reasoning: No mention of agents or autonomous AI systems acting on issues/PRs without a human submitter.

domains.suggested_improvement: no statement on energy/water/carbon impact of AI use
domains.reasoning: CONTRIBUTING.md contains no reference to energy, water, or carbon footprint concerns anywhere in the AI policy or elsewhere.

domains.suggested_improvement: no statement on server load or hardware cost from AI
domains.reasoning: No text addresses server load, hosting/hardware cost, or financing burden tied to AI tooling.

domains.suggested_improvement: no statement on project data being used to train models
domains.reasoning: No mention of Gitea's own issues, discussions, code, or user data being used (or restricted from use) to train AI models.

consent_policy_specificity.overall_posture: Gitea's CONTRIBUTING.md addresses AI use specifically and only for code contributions (PRs/issues) — requiring disclosure, human review before submission, and holding contributors accountable — while leaving notetaker bots, non-code content, moderation, review, autonomous use, environmental impact, infrastructure strain, and training data on project data entirely unaddressed.

awaiting_implementation.specific_tools_in_use: Awaiting implementation: named-product detection beyond known file signatures
awaiting_implementation.ai_tool_owner: Awaiting implementation: ownership and data control
awaiting_implementation.environmental_footprint: Awaiting implementation: model/system card and ESG disclosure
awaiting_implementation.proportionality: Awaiting implementation: resource use relative to contributor count (needs platform usage data)

use_composition_partial.note: Detection only. Absence of signal is not absence of use.

policy_change.blocker: Draft classifier not wired in or validated against hand-graded history. Repo.history() and Repo.commit_patch() supply the diffs.

use_compliance.blocker: Derived metric. Requires disclosed-use data (Use Composition) checked against the specificity grid. Composition is only partially detectable, so the comparison is not yet sound.

misuse.blocker: Not automatable. CHAOSS marks the core signals unknown: text-based AI detectors are unreliable, and license-laundering and wrongful-accusation incidents need maintainer self-report.
